prerequisites: Knowledge of physics phenomena and the laws of electrical engineering and physics
Series and parallel connection of electrical circuits

learning_outcomes.text: Use fundamental concepts of computer science and information technology.
Identify roles and responsibilities in a multidisciplinary team and apply effective relationship and work techniques within the team.
Model any multidisciplinary physical system and analyze it with a single simulation tool, such as the 20 SIM program.

syllabus_topics: The elements of bond graphs
The procedure of modeling electrical systems that are in stationary regime with the help of bond graphs.
The procedure of construction and modeling of electrical systems that are in alternating sinusoidal regime with the help of bond graphs.
Procedure for construction and modeling of bond graphs for three-phase electrical systems. Examples

Comparison of the results of electrical circuits that are in permanent sinusoidal regime solved using Kirchhoff's theorems with simulation results using the bond graphs and the simulation program 20 SIM

Comparison of the results of some electrical circuits that are in permanent sinusoidal regime solved using the theorem of cyclic currents with simulation results using the bond graphs and the simulation program 20 SIM

Comparison of the results of some electrical circuits that are in permanent sinusoidal regime solved using the theorem of the potentials at nodes with simulation results using the bond graphs and the simulation program 20 SIM
Causality on active elements and junction elements.
Causal loops. Causal ways.
Transmittance of active, passive elements, circuit transmittance. Mason's rule.
Frequency analysis of single-phase electrical circuits in alternating sinusoidal regime, using bond graphs using the 20 SIM simulation program
Frequency analysis of three-phase alternating sinusoidal electrical circuits using connection graphs using the 20 SIM simulation program
Calculation of transmittances for three-phase circuits applying Mason's Rule, using bond graphs
Modeling of electrical circuits that are in non-sinusoidal regime with the help of bond graphs
Calculation of transmittances for circuits that are in non-sinusoidal regime with the help of connection graphs. Examples
The procedure of construction and modeling of electrical systems that are in alternating sinusoidal regime with the help of bond graphs.

Comparison of the results of electrical circuits that are in permanent sinusoidal regime solved using Kirchhoff's theorems with simulation results using the bond graphs and the simulation program 20 SIM

Comparison of the results of some electrical circuits that are in permanent sinusoidal regime solved using the theorem of cyclic currents with simulation results using the bond graphs and the simulation program 20 SIM

Comparison of the results of some electrical circuits that are in permanent sinusoidal regime solved using the theorem of the potentials at nodes with simulation results using the bond graphs and the simulation program 20 SIM
Transmittance of active, passive elements, circuit transmittance. Mason's rule.
Frequency analysis of single-phase electrical circuits in alternating sinusoidal regime, using bond graphs using the 20 SIM simulation program
Frequency analysis of three-phase alternating sinusoidal electrical circuits using connection graphs using the 20 SIM simulation program

assessment_methods.method: Laboratory Activity oral or online simulation presentation

assessment_rules: The final grade (N) is calculated as 50% from the examination (Ex) and 50% from the seminar (S). To obtain credits, the final grade (N), the seminar (S), the laboratory (L), and the project (P) must each be greater than or equal to 5. Minimum performance standard: carrying out a work/project, responsibly performing tasks specific to the role in a multidisciplinary team.
